summary: The rewrite targets the right place: full decode_16/32 are 92-96% one gather kernel running at 2.67-2.94 TB/s against a 4.8 TB/s floor. Fusing to one launch and using stream-K are sound and should be worth about 10-15 us on their own. The spec has one definite indexing bug (new-token slots collide with segment slots) that will trip the self-check and silently fall back to master, so fix it before dispatch. Ship both BULK variants in the module so a miss on the bandwidth milestones can be attributed from a single run.
justification: Mechanism: FINDINGS shows full decode_16 = splitkv_attn 111.4 + combine 7.9 + pre 2.1 us (123.0 total, floor 63.2) and decode_32 = 245.5 + 8.6 + 2.3 (257.7, floor 126.4). Removing the pre and combine launches and the gaps (~11-12 us at B=16, ~12.5 us at B=32) is close to certain if the fused combine tail stays short. Stream-K over 64-token tiles removes the 1024-chunk quantization: about 1250 chunks over 264 CTAs is 4.73 vs 5 items, ~5%, which is plausible. The expected directions match TASK.md: the full shapes have weight 16 and are 67-78% of the decode_16/32 loads, while sliding, decode_1 and verify sit outside the config-only gate and should be flat. Numeric nits: with G = SM count = 132 (not 264), each request at B=16 spans ~8-9 CTAs, so ~10 slots, and ~5 at B=32, not the 17/9 stated. That is fewer, so the winner's merge is cheaper than budgeted. reference.generate_input fully permutes the pages (randperm over the whole pool), so every token costs two independent random 128-B row reads (K and V are separate tensors). Bytes in flight are not the limit: 8 stages x 16 KB per SM is ~17 MB GPU-wide against a Little's-law need of ~5 MB, and master already holds ~96 KB/SM in flight. So the move from 2.94 to 3.5 TB/s has to come from issue efficiency, sync removal or DRAM behaviour, not depth. WEAKEST LINK: the consumer side, more than the producer. One CTA per SM leaves 8 math warps per SM (2 per SMSP), where master has 16 (2 CTAs x 8 warps). At 3.5 TB/s each SM must retire one 16 KB tile every ~1200 cycles. Each consumer warp spends roughly 16 mma plus ~150-250 ALU instructions per tile (cvt e4m3->f16, byte_perm, ex2, shuffles, masks), all latency-bound chains. At 2 warps/SMSP, achieved IPC can drop far enough to make math, not memory, the limiter. The FP8 m16n8k32 QK halves the QK mma and removes the K converts, which helps, but V widening stays. Second weakest: cp.async.bulk at 128 B per op. TMA small-copy throughput on Hopper is the usual reason FA3/FlashInfer use cp.async for page-1 gathers, and the BULK=0 fallback correctly exists for this. Third: random-row DRAM/TLB efficiency (the 2.94 -> 2.67 drop between B=16 and B=32 at equal per-CTA work). This may cap even a perfect kernel near ~3.3-3.6 TB/s, so M3 is a stretch but M2 is physically reachable. The design can approach its floor in principle, and the correctness plan (synthetic self-check with grid 3, mid-request range boundaries, kv_scale 0.25, cache-row equality, counters back to zero) is adequate apart from the slot bug below.
confounders: The landed list for master's submission.py is empty, so no landed hypothesis confounds. The incumbent being replaced is master's own splitkv path (full-decode-cuda-gather-splitkv), and the milestones compare against its kernel times directly.

In flight, not landed: full-decode-cuda-fp8-qk-mma edits master's kernel A and uses the same FP8 QK math this rewrite adopts. If it lands before dispatch, the incumbent baseline shifts. Judge M1-M3 against whichever kernel A is master at dispatch (the hypothesis already says so), and read the rewrite's gain as structural (one launch, stream-K, producer), not as QK math.

In flight: sliding-deep-splits-on-cuda-splitkv may share or extend the splitkv module and its gating. The separate muse_full_ws_v1 module isolates the build, but the kernel_fn gate order (full_ws before splitkv) must be rechecked if that lands first.

Queued/held: fused-full-combine-normgate overlaps sub-change (4), the in-kernel combine plus epilogue. If this rewrite lands, that hypothesis is superseded for 1<B<=64 full decode and should be retired, not run on top.
interference: With nothing landed there is no ab-revert target, and for a kind: rewrite the next stage is the follow-up. The one real ambiguity in a single run is a miss on M1/M2: it could come from TMA small-copy issue (BULK=1) or from consumer latency at 1 CTA/SM. An extra check is not needed to resolve that. Instantiate the kernel as a template over BULK and build both into the one muse_full_ws_v1 module (one compile, ~same seconds). Gate on BULK=1 as planned. At import, after the self-check, run an eager synthetic timing of both instantiations (e.g. B=16 x 80K lens, cuda events, a few reps) and print the achieved TB/s for each, as a diagnostic only that does not select the path. That attributes the result from a single run, and stage 2 can flip BULK without a rebuild. A separate control companion would duplicate that information at the cost of a check, so none is proposed.
rules_flags: No rule violations in the design: FP8 E4M3 query (allowed), FP8 cache untouched in dtype, every key in [0, seq_lens[b]) plus the new token is attended, prefix/TP computed in-kernel (no host sync), grid from device properties, persistent counters are not derived from data (same pattern master uses), and the self-check runs at import on synthetic data, outside the timed call.

The new token's contribution must be computed from the ROUNDED values: k_fp8 dequantized times k_scale for the score, and v_fp8 for acc, scaled by v_scale at the end as for the gathered rows. The judge checks the output against the reference attending to your own written cache rows, so using the pre-rounding bf16 k/v from registers would add a systematic deviation. It would likely stay within bounds but needlessly.

Query rounding order: the spec rounds q AFTER multiplying by qk_scale_factor, while master and _splitkv_reference round BEFORE the scale. Both are E4M3 queries and both are allowed, but the self-check reference should match whichever the kernel does, or rel L2 includes a mismatch term.
Build budget: a second load_inline module adds about master's 41.5 s (logged) to the 15-minute run. Fine, but keep it to one module with both BULK instantiations rather than two modules.

Ticket correctness: if the expected count is too high, no CTA wins, the output stays uninitialized (garbage or NaN, failing the run) and counters never reset, which poisons later calls. If it is too low, the merge races. That is not a rule break, but it is why the 'counters back to 0' self-check item is essential. Also assert on empty CTA ranges (Ttot < G), which must not arrive on any ticket.
open_questions: SLOT COLLISION (fix before dispatch): segment slots are c + b for c in [0, G) and b in [0, B), so up to G + B - 2, and the new-token slots are 'grid + b', i.e. G .. G + B - 1. The last CTA always covers request B-1 at slot G + B - 2, which equals the new-token slot of request B-2. The same happens for other (c, b) near the end, so the self-check (grid 3, 7 requests) will fail and the run will silently measure master. Either offset the new-token slots to G + B - 1 + b, or, simpler and cheaper, fold the new token into the first-tile CTA's running state (initialize that warp's m = s_new, l = 1, acc = v_new), which removes the extra slot and the '+1' from the expected count.

Consumer occupancy: why 1 CTA/SM with 8 consumer warps rather than 2 CTAs/SM at ~100 KB each (e.g. 5-6 stages) or 12-16 consumer warps in one CTA? Master's 16 math warps per SM may be part of why it reaches 2.94 TB/s at all. If M1 fails, read the stall reasons (long scoreboard vs math pipe vs barrier) before changing the producer.
Slot counts per request: with G = 132 the stated ~17 (B=16) / ~9 (B=32) look like G = 264 numbers. Confirm the grid. If G = 264 (2 per SM) was intended, it contradicts '1 CTA per SM, ~147 KB'.

Zero-length requests: the judge's seq_lens are clamped to >= 1 (agentic) and >= 16 (mixed), but tiles_b = 0 leaves the new token with no owner. Define the owner as the CTA containing flat position TP_b (or the next nonempty one) so the kernel is total.

Masked rows 'zeroed once' do not stay zero once the ring is reused, so stale rows from earlier tiles remain. That is harmless only because the scores are masked to -inf (P = 0) and stale V is finite. State that the -inf mask, not zeroing, is the correctness mechanism.

Combine tail: the winner merges ~5-10 slots of 16x64 fp32 from L2 with .cg plus the epilogue, ~1-3 us on the critical path after the last CTA. Report the kernel's own time minus a no-combine variant only if M2 is missed narrowly.
